diagram_math_checks.objects_and_maps: M_{n-1}=int D² minus the first n−1 ordered base points, based at q_n. i sends x to (q_1,…,q_{n−1},x), landing in F_n(int D²), based at q. p and p^D forget the last coordinate into F_{n−1}(int D²) and F_{n−1}(D²), based at q′.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Statement and step 1.3; supplier thm-fadell-neuwirth-forgetful-fibration part 1 identifies the fibre. Distinctness of q makes i well-defined. For a based loop γ in the punctured disc, iγ keeps the first n−1 points fixed and moves the last along γ.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The square commutes: p^D ∘ iota_n^F = iota_{n−1}^F ∘ p. Also p ∘ i is constant at q′.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Both paths in the square send (x_1,…,x_n) to the same first n−1 coordinates in the closed-disc configuration space (step 1.2). Substitution in i gives p(i(x))=q′. The arrows are directed open-to-closed, never reversed.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The vertical inclusions induce fundamental-group isomorphisms at the same q and q′; κ=(iota_n^F)_* i_* and φ=(p^D)_*.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Local supplier lem-interior-and-closed-disk-configuration-spaces-are-homotopy-equivalent claim 3 and local definition def-pure-braid-group-from-ordered-configurations fix PB_m in the closed-disc convention. Steps 1.2 and 3.1 apply functoriality to these same based inclusions; no basepoint path is silently chosen.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The displayed group row is short exact: κ injective, im κ=ker φ, φ surjective.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Step 1.1 uses the local punctured-disc wedge supplier and planar-configuration pi_2 supplier: π₂(base)=0 and π₀(fibre) is one point. Step 2.1 obtains injectivity, kernel/image equality and surjectivity from the fibration LES; step 3.1 transports them. F_{n−1} is the fibre fundamental group, not a configuration space. No section, splitting, action, chosen meridian paths, crossings, or orientation assertion is added. The first-then-second loop convention is preserved.
